english: is that how you treat me?
also: is that the way to behave?

terms.gloss: is that how you behave? so that’s your game?
is this how …? so this is the way …? (opening a reproach)
terms.register: vōx plērumque cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; semel Cic.
evidence: Plaut. Merc. 158: Sīcine mī obsequēns es?
terms.comment: Sīc with the question particle -ne. It always opens the sentence and almost always implies a reproach; frequent in the comic writers, once in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Sīcine mī obsequēns es? — Quid vīs faciam?
phrases.english: Is this how you oblige me? — What do you want me to do?

phrases.latin: Sīcine hoc fit? forās aedibus mē ējicī?
phrases.english: Is this how it goes? Me, thrown out of the house?

short-e.html: The last syllable is the question particle -ne, which is short (Lewis & Short -nĕ). Catull. 64.132, sīcine mē patriīs āvectam, perfide, ab ārīs: the word opens the hexameter as a dactyl. So too 64.134 and 77.3, which Lewis & Short cites.
